title: Integrated Population Balance and Multiphysics Modeling for Predicting Undesired Agglomeration in Small Molecule Manufacturing
authors: Prakitr Srisuma, Peter Hou, Shashank Venkat Muddu, Neda Nazemifard, Allan S. Myerson, Richard D. Braatz
abstract: Agitated filter dryers (AFDs) are a crucial unit operation in small molecule manufacturing that enables simultaneous filtration, washing, and drying of active pharmaceutical ingredients. One of the key challenges in AFDs is associated with undesired agglomeration, where the presence of hard agglomerates results in off-spec products, equipment damage, and additional downstream processing. This article presents a novel mechanistic model that describes the formation of soft and hard agglomerates during agitated filter drying. By integrating population balance and multiphysics modeling, the model can accurately predict the evolution of the product temperature, moisture content, and particle size distribution, and hence quantify the extend and impact of undesired agglomeration across various operating conditions. Our proposed model-based framework enables the rational design and operation of AFDs for improving the product quality and process reliability.
summary: This paper presents a sophisticated, integrated model combining Population Balance Modeling with multiphysics simulation to predict particle agglomeration in agitated filter dryers used for drug manufacturing. By distinguishing between soft and hard agglomerates, the framework allows engineers to rationally design and operate the drying process to maintain high product quality and reliability.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is predicting and mitigating undesired hard agglomeration of small molecules during the critical agitated filter drying (AFD) process in pharmaceutical manufacturing.
main_result: The developed model successfully predicts the evolution of particle size distribution (PSD) and quantifies the impact of agglomeration, showing that process parameters like mass transfer rates can be tuned to minimize hard agglomerate formation.
method: The study employs a novel mechanistic model that couples Population Balance Modeling (PBM) with multiphysics simulations to track heat, mass, and particle size changes simultaneously.
model_or_system: The physical system is an Agitated Filter Dryer (AFD) used for drying Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). The model integrates energy and mass balances with PBM to account for soft and hard agglomeration/breakage kinetics.
key_observables: Product temperature, moisture content, particle size distribution (PSD), and the quantification of soft vs. hard agglomerates.
important_parameters: Solubility, mass transfer rates, and the ratio of liquid evaporation rate to solid growth rate govern the agglomeration kinetics.
main_assumptions: The system is assumed to be well-mixed due to continuous agitation, and the model explicitly distinguishes between soft (liquid bridge) and hard (solid bridge) agglomerates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the AFD experimental setup, the mechanistic model components (heat/mass transfer, PBM), and the time evolution of particle size percentiles (D90, D99) under different conditions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of agglomeration in AFDs, presents the coupled PBM/multiphysics framework (including energy/mass balances and specific kinetic terms for agglomeration/breakage), validates the model against experimental data (both limiting and practical cases), and concludes with parametric studies for process optimization.
why_interesting: While the application is chemical engineering, the rigorous coupling of population dynamics (PBM) with coupled transport phenomena (heat/mass transfer) and kinetic rate laws shares mathematical formalism with modeling complex non-equilibrium systems in condensed matter physics.
